findings.evidence: 1. Pin down the requested behavior, the runtime/framework and the architectural layer. ... 2. Search on the behavior and its synonyms ... 4. Read each promising file and extract the smallest self-contained section that works
findings.fix: Cut steps 1, 2 and 4 down to the parts the model would not do by itself: always open callers and tests, and keep a snippet small but complete. The model already knows to search with synonyms and read the files it finds. Use the freed lines for repository-specific signals, such as how to tell generated or vendored copies apart from maintained code.

findings.evidence: Pattern types to cover when relevant: feature, structural, integration, testing.
findings.fix: Add a decision rule that maps the request to pattern types, for example: 'how do we call X' -> integration + testing; 'where does Y live' -> structural; otherwise feature + testing. This turns the list of types into a way of thinking about the request.

findings.evidence: ## Gotchas has two items (.gitignore-hidden scope, mock-only tests)
findings.fix: Add one more trap that runs against expectation: a barrel or re-export file (index.ts, __init__.py) often matches first and looks like the definition. Follow it to the defining file before you cite it, or the caller will copy an import path instead of the code.

findings.evidence: Report one example per materially distinct approach ... at most 3 variations per pattern type, unless the caller asks for more. / Never ... rank
findings.fix: Resolve what happens when there are more than 3 distinct approaches without ranking them. For example: 'If more than 3 distinct approaches exist, show the 3 with the most call sites (state the count), and list the rest by file:line under Related Utilities with "N further approaches not expanded".' Also say what to do when the request names no clear behavior: report the interpretation you assumed at the top of the report.
